Definition: {to go (causatively, bring) out, in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively, direct and proxim.}
BiblicalUsage: In the Bible, yᵉtsâʼ means to go out. In Ezra 6:15, this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar.
TheologicalSignificance: The house was finished and the work went out into the open, and I hold that yᵉtsâʼ marks the moment hidden labour becomes visible.
